lines.text: 'A humming room under the meat hall…'
'…that the students built, and forgot.'
Have you read anything that good? I haven't.
Nobody has judged the yam. I'll wait.
…Does anybody want yam?
Have you read anything good? No? Come in. Sit. Yam?
Hello. What's on your shelf? Be honest. Textbooks don't count.
Sannu. [Hello.] I saved you a book. And some yam. Separately.
Go. Read on the shuttle. It makes the road shorter.
Thank you. That deserves a bookmark. Here.
You returned it on time. With no coffee rings. Marry a librarian.
Your shelf has one novel. It's a phone charger box.
You read the last page first. I can tell. It's in your face.
Pardon? I was in chapter nine. Say it to chapter one.
Who? There was nobody there fa. You've been reading too many novels.
No. I don't lend that one. It came back with jollof on page twelve once.
Have you read… anything? This year? A menu counts. Barely.
Why did the book join the gym? To work on its spine. Yam?
Careful. That's a first edition. You're a later edition. Fine.
'It was a dark and stormy night…' Light's gone. Perfect timing. Yam?
Rain on the bookshop roof. Best sound on campus. Stay.
Roasted yam. Hot. From the woman by the gate. Have half. Have all.
A bookmark! Thank you. My books thank you. They were lonely.
An e-reader. Thank you. I'll use it as a coaster.
An old book! Look at the binding! Smell it! …Don't tell anyone I sniffed it.
'…and the rains came early that year, and nobody was ready.'
Biography. Poetry. Yam recipes. That's a shelf.
'The library at night keeps its own counsel.' Somebody wrote that. I'll find who.
Fresher! What are you reading? Your timetable doesn't count.
First years buy the textbook, then sell it back unopened. Every year.
You matriculated in a gown made for two. I put it in my notebook.
Your first essay. 'In conclusion' three times. Choose one conclusion.
'A humming room under the meat hall.' I still read it at night.
The archive. Three departments, one story. We found it with dust and patience.
You read the ledger like a novel. That's a skill. Nobody has it.
You've started a business. And a radio show. And stopped reading. I noticed.
Strike. Bookshop open. One customer. Me. I'm buying everything.
The tape machine. Her voice. Have you read anything that brave? I haven't.
The tape machine was under my bed, behind the yam sack. Glad I keep both.
Strike month six. I've reread every book. Even the bad ones. Especially.
Cook-off. I entered yam. Only yam. It's a statement.
Nobody judged the yam. I waited. I'm still waiting.
You checked before you shared. Like a good reader. Like an editor.
Your column in the twins' chart. I read it. Twice. It needs editing.
My book. Printed in the market. Two hundred copies. Forty sold. All to Mum.
'Thank you for the lamp.' Off the night noticeboard. No name. I kept it.
The notebook. Everyone was so quiet. I offered yam. It helped.
You'll be in my next book. Kindly. Mostly kindly.
Convocation. Keep a book in your bag. Always. Yam is optional.
Freshers! Bookshop sale! Second-hand textbooks with first-hand notes!
Exam week. Everyone wants the book I've had on the shelf for a year.
Market day! The book man by the tailor has poetry. Old poetry. I'm going!
Convocation. Gowns everywhere. Like a library came to life.
Iftar. I'm bringing yam. I'm always bringing yam.
Christmas break. Shop shut. I've taken six books home. And yam.
Harmattan. The old pages crack. I wrap them in cloth. Like babies.
